sections.heading: Metal Roofs vs. Other Roofing Materials: Benefits and the Biggest Problem

runs.v: Commercial metal roofing offers excellent weather resistance against snow and wind and can stand up to hail and the elements; snow sheds from smooth panels, limiting ice dams, and commercial metal roofs often carry a Class A fire rating for fire safety. The benefits over asphalt shingles and other roofing materials: durability, longevity, reliable performance, and low maintenance; reflective metal coatings improve a building's energy efficiency and can significantly reduce cooling costs in summer, and commercial metal roofs are often 100% recyclable and contain recycled content. Galvalume steel combines aluminum and zinc for corrosion resistance, barrel metal roofing resembles curved tiles, and metal roofing systems are compatible with solar installations and heavy equipment. The biggest problem with metal roofs sits at fasteners and seams: exposed fasteners back out as washers weather, and steel corrodes where a coating breaks, so minor repairs and prompt roof repair after storm damage protect the investment. faqs.q: How long does a commercial metal roof last on an Orange building?

runs.v: 40 to 80 years: standing seam 40 to 70, exposed-fastener about 30 to 50, and copper 70-plus, per InterNACHI and This Old House.

faqs.q: Is metal roofing appropriate for a flat converted-industrial roof in the Valley Arts area?

runs.v: Only with at least ¼ inch per foot of slope, per NRCA and ARMA; a truly flat roof is better served by TPO, EPDM, or modified bitumen, and a survey confirms the slope before fabrication.

faqs.q: Does a commercial metal roof in an Orange historic district need a Certificate of Appropriateness?

runs.v: It can: properties in a locally designated historic district can need extra review before exterior roofing work, separate from the permit. Confirm a parcel's status with the City of Orange Township before work.

faqs.q: What is the 25% rule, and do you need a permit for a commercial metal roof in Orange, NJ?

runs.v: Yes: the ordinary-maintenance exemption under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 covers repair of no more than 25% of the roof area in 12 months, so a commercial metal roof replacement needs a permit. Complete removal applies when the roof is water-soaked or carries 2 or more layers, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4.
